eligibility.quote: The issue is with the action client, not with BufferClient (state is available before result).

failed_conditions.quote: The issue is with the action client, not with BufferClient (state is available before result). I created a simplified case without using bufferclient, which I will post along with an issue in actionlib when I have cleaned it up.

Cranking the rate up to 100000 I was also able to get a double answer: 

[ERROR] [WallTime: 1464801977.428899] Received comm state ACTIVE when in simple state DONE with SimpleActionClient in NS /tf2_buffer_server
[ERROR] [WallTime: 1464801978.438880] SimpleActionClient received DONE twice

loudness.quote: raise tf2.TransformException("The BufferServer returned None for result or result.error!  Something is likely wrong with the server.")

resolution.quote: From this short test I believe that the problem was partially mitigated. In fact, no more tf errors are thrown, however there is still something wrong with the tf state machine.

notes: All quotes verified verbatim against the issue body and comments 223066155 (tfoote), 431658241 (g-gemignani), 431801344 (jorgenfb), and the fix commit 566092b (diff matches '- state == GoalStatus.SUCCEEDED or state == GoalStatus.LOST:' -> '+ state == GoalStatus.LOST:' and '+ if state == GoalStatus.SUCCEEDED and self.client.get_result(): return True'). Both failed conditions are genuinely class 'other' (state/result ordering and the provider's internal DONE-twice state machine have no matching named class). Loudness silent/run is correct: the only diagnostic is the consumer's own TransformException at run time. Resolution 'observed' is defensible because the reporter re-ran the reproducer with/without the patch; the spec honestly notes the residual actionlib state-machine errors and the unstated actionlib revision.
